Chapter 7: Advancing Others — The Principle of Increase
As we keep building on this framework, there's a powerful idea that really stands out. True wealth? It's not just about what you can get for yourself—it's about how much you can help others grow, too.
That’s the heart of the principle of increase. When you show up to every conversation, every deal, and even the smallest interactions, with a real intention to leave people better than you found them, you’re actually lining yourself up with something bigger—the creative energy of the universe.
Think about it: life naturally wants to expand, to get better. When you help others move forward—maybe by offering a helping hand, sharing encouragement, or creating real value—you become a channel for abundance. Not just for them, but for yourself, too.
Let me paint you a picture. Imagine a gardener who cares for their own plot, but also shares seeds and advice with neighbors. As every garden starts to thrive, the whole neighborhood blossoms. And you know what? That gardener’s own harvest gets richer, thanks to everyone’s shared success.
So, how can you start living out the principle of increase? Here are a few simple ways:
Look for ways to add value, even in quick chats or small favors.
Offer genuine praise, or share resources that help someone move forward.
And whether it’s work or personal life, lead with generosity and a desire to serve.
Picture a manager who puts real effort into developing their team—mentoring, giving them chances to shine, and celebrating their wins. As the team succeeds, the whole company gets stronger. And the manager? Their reputation and influence just keep on growing.
This principle works with what you offer to the world, too. When you deliver a product or service that’s worth more than what people pay, you earn their trust, loyalty, and respect. Over time, that reputation brings even more opportunities your way, setting off a cycle of growth that feeds itself.
Now, here’s something important: the principle of increase isn’t about forgetting your own needs, or giving so much you’re left empty. It’s about understanding that your own success is deeply connected to the success of those around you.
When you make it your mission to help everyone you meet move forward, you’re tapping into the same expansive energy that fuels real, lasting prosperity.
